subject: Neighborhood Ambassador Task Force
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn and Task Force Chair Milva McDonald on Medford Happenings. The discussion focused on the recent opening of Carr Park and the creation, goals, and structure of the newly formed Neighborhood Ambassador Task Force.

items.title: Carr Park Ribbon Cutting
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn highlighted the final ribbon cutting for Carr Park, including the opening of a splash pad and solar-powered shade covers funded with federal and ARPA assistance.

items.title: Neighborhood Ambassador Task Force Origins and Purpose
items.summary: The Mayor and Milva McDonald explained that the task force was established to improve two-way communication between City Hall and residents across different neighborhoods.

items.title: Task Force Member Selection and Leadership
items.summary: The Mayor detailed selecting approximately two applicants per neighborhood from a public call, resulting in a volunteer group of over 13 members chaired by McDonald.

items.title: Task Force Goals, Outreach, and Initiatives
items.summary: McDonald and the Mayor discussed early goals to familiarize ambassadors with city resources, share survey information, and coordinate with municipal departments such as Outreach and the Board of Health.

items.title: Upcoming Events and Program Structure
items.summary: McDonald noted the task force will table at the farmers market on September 10, support a fall library card drive, and potentially hold a library open house, operating as an informal volunteer advisory group without term limits.

items.title: Target Audience and Program Impact
items.summary: The Mayor and McDonald stated that the program is aimed primarily at residents who miss traditional communications, while serving as a collaborative resource for city staff.
